rules: No mass noindex; no deletion; no redirect in this plan.
Similarity >= 0.80 nominates canonical candidates only (R-CANON-1 v1.1.0).
Every wave is reversible by reverting one commit, and is sized so its effect is measurable in isolation.
No traffic, indexation or backlink figure is asserted: none is held in this repository.

canonical_consolidation.conclusion: No canonical change is safe today: pointing duplicates at a destination that itself fails Gate 12 consolidates signals onto a thin page. Rebuild a destination first (KO), then consolidate.

wave_1.change: robots 'index, follow' -> 'noindex, follow'; remove the 15 URLs from sitemap-terms-*.xml; body, canonical and links unchanged; pages stay reachable (HTTP 200)
wave_1.why_this_family: Objective, reviewable criteria (atomic number >= 104; PubChem exact-name miss; Gate 12 FAIL; no inbound internal links found in site/public). Identity cannot be verified, so there is nothing to rebuild from evidence.
wave_1.simulated_gate: With the 15 robots changes applied to a copy of site/public, validate_publication_authority reports only the pre-existing /acquire/ block; RL debt drops 14032 -> 14017.
preconditions: Search Console export for the 15 URLs (Page indexing + Performance, last 16 months). Any URL with clicks > 0, or reported as linked externally, is removed from the wave and re-reviewed
/acquire/ decision applied or approved first (otherwise the deploy gate stays red)

quality: only the robots line and sitemap entries change (diff review)
authority gate PASS; Gate 12 surface counts unchanged except RL debt -15
indexation: Search Console 'Excluded by noindex' rises by at most 15 within 4–8 weeks
no change in indexing status of non-wave URLs
traffic: site-level clicks/impressions compared 28 days before vs after; wave URLs' clicks expected near zero
abort_if: any non-wave URL drops out of the index without cause
owner or Search Console shows the wave URLs carried traffic

wave_1.rollback: git revert of the wave commit (restores robots + sitemap lines), redeploy, request recrawl in Search Console; no data lost because no page is removed
wave_1.governance_gap: The deploy gate allows any robots DOWNGRADE without an approved decision (verified by simulation). Approval of a wave is therefore enforced by review, not by the gate. Proposed follow-up: the gate should require an approved url_decision for every legacy downgrade (except ledger-derived ones). CLOSED in Release-01 PR-A: the gate now blocks any discretionary downgrade or sitemap removal without an approved, signed url_decision (BLOCK_UNAPPROVED_DOWNGRADE / BLOCK_UNAPPROVED_SITEMAP_REMOVAL).
